title: Writing at B2: the opinion piece, the complaint, the report
title_target: Då blir det ett resonemang i stället för en lista.
goal: Plan and write a Swedish debattartikel, a formal complaint and a short report, using paragraphs and connectors that make the text hang together.
bekal: you can build a *debattartikel*: headline, lead, thesis, arguments, counterargument, demand
you can tie sentences together with reference words (*detta*, *denna*, *sådan*) and connectors by function
you can switch to a formal written register for complaints and reports
wave: Go back to Unit 11: take any five sentences from that unit's debate and rewrite them as one paragraph, using one connector for adding (*dessutom*), one for contrast (*däremot*) and one for concluding (*alltså*).

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Vid köksbordet
dialogs.intro: A Sunday evening in the Södermalm flat. Dian has written an opinion piece about car-free streets and wants to send it to a Stockholm newspaper's debate page tonight. Elin, who reads more than anyone Dian knows, picks up the printout.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Är det här din debattartikel? Får jag läsa?
lines.id: Is this your opinion piece? Can I read it?
lines.literal: is it here your debate-article? may I read?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Gärna, men var snäll. Jag ska skicka den till tidningens debattsida ikväll.
lines.id: Please do, but be kind. I'm sending it to the paper's debate page tonight.
lines.literal: gladly, but be kind. I shall send it to newspaper-the's debate-page tonight.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Rubriken är bra — kort och tydlig. Men ingressen är för lång. Där ska tesen stå, i en enda mening.
lines.id: The headline is good — short and clear. But the lead is too long. That's where your thesis goes, in one single sentence.
lines.literal: headline-the is good — short and clear. but lead-the is too long. there shall thesis-the stand, in one single sentence.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Okej. Och resten? Hänger argumenten ihop?
lines.id: OK. And the rest? Do the arguments hang together?
lines.literal: okay. and rest-the? hang arguments-the together?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: För det mesta. Men här hoppar du från luftföroreningar till barns lek utan någon övergång.
lines.id: Mostly. But here you jump from air pollution to children's play without any transition.
lines.literal: for the most. but here jump you from air-pollutions to children's play without any transition.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jag kan väl lägga till "Dessutom handlar det om…"?
lines.id: I could just add "Moreover, it's about…", couldn't I?
lines.literal: I can surely add to "moreover deals it about…"?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Ja, eller ännu bättre: knyt ihop dem. Renare luft är ju också en fråga om barnens hälsa.
lines.id: Yes, or even better: tie them together. Cleaner air is also a question of children's health, after all.
lines.literal: yes, or even better: tie together them. cleaner air is you-know also a question about children-the's health.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Smart. Då blir det ett resonemang i stället för en lista.
lines.id: Clever. Then it becomes a line of reasoning instead of a list.
lines.literal: smart. then becomes it a reasoning in place-the for a list.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Precis. Och du måste bemöta motargumenten. Vad säger handlarna i innerstan?
lines.id: Exactly. And you have to respond to the counterarguments. What do the shopkeepers in the city center say?
lines.literal: exactly. and you must meet counter-arguments-the. what say traders-the in inner-city-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Att de förlorar kunder. Men studier pekar snarare åt motsatt håll — det har jag med i fjärde stycket.
lines.id: That they'll lose customers. But studies rather point the other way — I've got that in the fourth paragraph.
lines.literal: that they lose customers. but studies point rather towards opposite direction — that have I with in fourth paragraph-the.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Flytta upp det. Och avsluta med ett konkret krav, inte bara "vi måste tänka om".
lines.id: Move it up. And finish with a concrete demand, not just "we need to rethink".
lines.literal: move up it. and finish with a concrete demand, not only "we must think again".

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ett krav till politikerna, alltså. Okej, jag skriver om slutet.
lines.id: A demand to the politicians, then. OK, I'll rewrite the ending.
lines.literal: a demand to politicians-the, so. okay, I write over end-the.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Och stryk hälften av alla "väldigt" och "mycket". Texten blir starkare utan dem.
lines.id: And cut half of all the "very"s and "really"s. The text gets stronger without them.
lines.literal: and strike half-the of all "very" and "much". text-the becomes stronger without them.

notes: **En debattartikel** (**en deh-BAHT-ah-ti-kel**) is an opinion piece written by an outside contributor — a researcher, an organization, an engaged citizen. Swedish newspapers publish several every day, and the format is strict: about 3,000–4,500 characters, a clear thesis, and a concrete demand at the end. *DN Debatt* is the most famous forum.

**Ingressen** (**in-GRES-sen**) is the lead paragraph under the headline, usually in bold. In a debattartikel it states the thesis and names the writer in the third person: *…, skriver Dian, konsult inom hållbar stadsutveckling.* The editors often write it, but it pays to suggest one yourself.

**Hänga ihop** (**HENG-ah ee-HOOP**) — to hang together, be coherent; **knyta ihop** (**KNÜ-tah ee-HOOP**) — to tie together. *Sammanhang* (connection, context) and *sammanhängande* (coherent) come from the same idea. Particle stress (Unit 8): the stress falls on *ihop*.

**Ett resonemang** (**et reh-soo-neh-MAHNG**), a French loan, is a line of reasoning — the opposite of a list of points. Elin's advice is central to Swedish school writing: link each argument to the previous one instead of just stacking them with *dessutom*.

**Bemöta** (**beh-MÖ-tah**) means to respond to, rebut (an argument or criticism); compare *möta* (to meet). **Snarare** (rather) softens the claim: *studier pekar snarare åt motsatt håll* is more careful than *forskningen visar motsatsen* — the hedging of Unit 4 in action.

**Skriva om** (**SKREE-vah OM**, stress on the particle) = to rewrite; *skriva **om** något* with the stress on the verb means "to write about something". **Stryka** (**STRÜ-kah**) = to strike out, delete — the editor's favorite verb.

grammars.title: The anatomy of a debattartikel
body: Swedish opinion pieces follow a recognizable pattern. Readers and editors expect it, so using it makes you sound competent before they have read a word of your argument.

head: Part
Swedish name
What it does
Typical phrase
rows: states the demand or thesis, often as an imperative
thesis in one or two sentences + who writes
a concrete picture of the problem
two or three, each in its own paragraph
why the objection does not hold
what exactly should happen, by whom

after: Use **bör** (should, ought to) for recommendations in writing: *Staden bör införa…*, *Försöket bör utvärderas.* It is more formal and more objective than *borde*, which sounds like a personal opinion or regret.
Swedish argument texts prefer short paragraphs (*stycken*) of three to five sentences, each opened by a **kärnmening** (topic sentence) that tells the reader what the paragraph is about.

dialogs.title: Text — Ge gatorna tillbaka till barnen
dialogs.intro: This is the final version of Dian's article, as it appeared in the newspaper three days later. Read it with the anatomy table beside you, and underline every word that ties one sentence to the next.

lines.speaker: Rubrik:
lines.text: Ge innerstadens gator tillbaka till barnen
lines.id: Give the inner-city streets back to the children
lines.literal: give inner-city-the's streets back to children-the

lines.speaker: Ingress:
lines.text: Stockholm bör stänga innerstadens bostadsgator för biltrafik på helgerna. Det skulle ge renare luft, tryggare barn och ett mer levande stadsliv, skriver Dian, konsult inom hållbar stadsutveckling.
lines.id: Stockholm should close the inner city's residential streets to cars at weekends. It would give cleaner air, safer children and a livelier city, writes Dian, a consultant in sustainable urban development.
lines.literal: Stockholm ought close … for car-traffic on weekends-the. it would give cleaner air, safer children and a more living city-life, writes Dian, consultant within sustainable city-development.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Varje helg fylls Södermalms gator av bilar som letar parkering. Samtidigt saknar många barn en trygg plats att leka på nära hemmet.
lines.id: Every weekend Södermalm's streets fill up with cars looking for parking. At the same time, many children lack a safe place to play near home.
lines.literal: every weekend is-filled Södermalm's streets of cars that search parking. at-the-same-time lack many children a safe place to play on near home-the.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Biltrafiken står för en stor del av luftföroreningarna i innerstaden. Detta drabbar framför allt barn, vars lungor fortfarande utvecklas.
lines.id: Car traffic accounts for a large share of the air pollution in the inner city. This hits children above all, whose lungs are still developing.
lines.literal: car-traffic-the stands for a large part of … this strikes before all children, whose lungs still develop-themselves.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Renare luft är alltså inte bara en miljöfråga, utan också en folkhälsofråga.
lines.id: Cleaner air is thus not only an environmental issue but also a public health issue.
lines.literal: cleaner air is thus not only an environment-question, but also a public-health-question.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Dessutom visar erfarenheter från städer som Barcelona och Oslo att bilfria gator blir mötesplatser där grannar lär känna varandra.
lines.id: Moreover, experience from cities like Barcelona and Oslo shows that car-free streets become meeting places where neighbors get to know each other.
lines.literal: moreover show experiences from cities like … that car-free streets become meeting-places where neighbors learn know each-other.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Kritiker invänder att handeln skulle förlora kunder. Den oron är förståelig, men studier från flera europeiska städer pekar snarare åt motsatt håll.
lines.id: Critics object that shops would lose customers. That concern is understandable, but studies from several European cities rather point the other way.
lines.literal: critics object that trade-the would lose customers. that worry-the is understandable, but studies … point rather towards opposite direction.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Fotgängare och cyklister handlar visserligen mindre åt gången, men de kommer tillbaka oftare.
lines.id: Pedestrians and cyclists admittedly buy less at a time, but they come back more often.
lines.literal: pedestrians and cyclists shop admittedly less at time-the, but they come back more-often.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Jag föreslår därför att staden inför bilfria helger på tre gator på Södermalm, som ett försök under nästa sommar.
lines.id: I therefore propose that the city introduce car-free weekends on three streets on Södermalm, as a trial next summer.
lines.literal: I propose therefore that city-the introduces car-free weekends … as a trial during next summer.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Försöket bör utvärderas av en oberoende part innan beslut fattas om en permanent förändring.
lines.id: The trial should be evaluated by an independent party before any decision is taken on a permanent change.
lines.literal: trial-the ought be-evaluated by an independent party before decision is-taken about a permanent change.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Gatorna är stadens största offentliga rum. Det är dags att vi delar dem rättvist.
lines.id: The streets are the city's largest public space. It's time we shared them fairly.
lines.literal: streets-the are city-the's largest public rooms. it is time that we share them fairly.

notes: **Varje helg fylls … gatorna** — *fyllas* (to be filled, fill up) is an s-passive with no agent needed; the *av*-phrase (*av bilar*) names what fills them. Starting with a concrete scene, not an abstract claim, is a classic opening move.

**Detta drabbar framför allt barn** — *detta* (this) refers back to the whole previous sentence. In writing, Swedes prefer *detta* to *det* when the reference is a whole idea; *det* could be misread as pointing to one noun. **Drabba** (**DRAHB-bah**) = to hit, affect (negatively): *drabbas av* = to be hit by.

**Vars lungor** — *vars* (whose) is the written relative pronoun for possession (Svenska 102, Unit 13). In speech many people avoid it (*barn som fortfarande har lungor som utvecklas*), but in a newspaper text it is exactly right.
**Inte bara …, utan också …** — not only … but also. Note **utan** (not *men*) after a negation: *inte en miljöfråga **utan** en folkhälsofråga*. This is one of the most common errors at B2 level.

**Visserligen …, men …** (**VIS-ser-lee-gen**) — "admittedly …, but …": you grant the opponent a point and then turn it. *Visserligen* sits in the sentence-adverb slot after the verb, and the *men*-clause carries your real message.

**Innan beslut fattas** — *fatta beslut* (to take a decision) is the standard collocation; the s-passive *fattas* keeps the focus on the decision, not on who makes it. **Det är dags att vi delar** — after *det är dags att*, Swedish uses an ordinary present tense where English uses "it's time we shared".

grammars.title: Cohesion: tying sentences together
body: A B2 text is not judged on single sentences but on how they connect. Two kinds of tools do the work: reference words that point back, and connectors that show the logical relation.

head: Function
Connectors and reference words
Example
rows: **detta, denna, dessa, en sådan, den här**

after: Connectors are adverbs, not conjunctions: when one opens the sentence it takes the first position, so the verb follows and the subject moves behind it — *Dessutom **visar** erfarenheter…*, *Därför **föreslår** jag…* (Unit 1). Placed after the verb, the same words often sound smoother in the middle of a paragraph: *Jag föreslår **därför**…*.

Follow the known → new principle: begin each sentence with something the reader already knows (*Detta*, *Den oron*, *Försöket*) and end with the new information. That alone makes a text feel connected.

blocks.text: Swedish formal letters are friendlier than English ones: most begin with a simple **Hej** (or *Hej [name]*); *Bästa* is a slightly more formal option, while *Bäste* and *Till den det berör* now sound old-fashioned. What makes a complaint formal is the structure and precision, not stiff phrasing. A complaint about a faulty product is called a **reklamation**; consumers in Sweden have the right to complain about faults for three years after purchase, and an independent board, *Allmänna reklamationsnämnden* (ARN), handles disputes for free.

head: Step
Phrase
English
rows: Den 3 oktober beställde jag… Den 10 oktober upptäckte jag att…
On October 3 I ordered… On October 10 I discovered that…
Trots upprepade kontakter har felet inte åtgärdats.
Despite repeated contacts, the fault has not been fixed.
Jag kräver därför att… / Jag ber er därför att…
I therefore demand that… / I therefore ask you to…
Jag ser fram emot ert svar senast den 15 november.
I look forward to your reply by November 15 at the latest.

blocks.title: Formal word swaps
items: *funka* → **fungera** · *fixa* → **åtgärda** · *grej* → **vara**, **produkt**
*få tillbaka pengarna* → **få pengarna återbetalda** · *snabbt* → **snarast**
*om* (about) → **angående**, **gällande** · *alltså* (spoken filler) → leave out
Write *ni / er* to a company — it is the normal plural "you", not old-fashioned politeness.

blocks.text: At work Dian writes short reports (*rapporter*, *PM*) all the time. The Swedish standard structure is so fixed that readers jump straight to the part they need — usually the conclusions. Use headings, keep paragraphs short, and write in *klarspråk* (Unit 6): active verbs, everyday words, one idea per sentence.

head: Heading
Content
Typical phrase
rows: the whole report in five lines
*Kommunen har gett oss i uppdrag att…*
what the report aims to find out
what it means and what should be done

blocks.title: Paragraphing rules of thumb
items: One idea per paragraph, opened by a topic sentence (*kärnmening*).
Mark a new paragraph either with a blank line or with an indent — not both.
Keep connectors varied: three *dessutom* in a row is a sign that the text is a list, not a line of reasoning.
Read the text aloud. Where you run out of breath, the sentence is too long.

exercises.title: Connectors
exercises.prompt: Fill in a suitable connector: *dessutom, däremot, visserligen, alltså, därför, slutligen*. Use each once.
items: Bilarna förorenar luften. ____ tar de plats från barnen.
Handlarna är oroliga. Forskningen visar ____ att de inte förlorar kunder.
____ handlar cyklister mindre, men de kommer oftare.
Luften blir renare och barnen friskare. Förslaget är ____ bra för folkhälsan.
Trafiken ökar varje år. ____ måste staden agera nu.
____ vill jag betona att försöket är tillfälligt.

items: I therefore propose a trial.

answers: Dessutom — däremot — Visserligen — alltså — Därför — Slutligen
Detta drabbar framför allt barn. — Försöket bör utvärderas av en oberoende part. — Jag föreslår därför bilfria helger. — Argumenten hänger inte ihop. — Kritiker invänder att handeln förlorar kunder.
Jag skriver angående varan som jag köpte. — Den fungerar inte. — Jag ber er att åtgärda felet snarast. — Jag kräver att få pengarna återbetalda. — Jag ser fram emot ert svar senast på fredag.
Jag föreslår därför ett försök. — Den oron är förståelig. — Du måste bemöta motargumenten. — Avsluta med ett konkret krav. — Det är inte bara en miljöfråga, utan också en folkhälsofråga.
